newsitem.title: UK: Russia bond prompts trade in country's other debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia bond prompts trade in country's other debt.

text.p: Emerging market debt focussed on Russian risk following the launch of a $2.0 billion 10-year bond for the country, dealers said on Thursday.
"In the Russian loan market we saw strength as investors bought into Russia on the back of the $2.0 billion issue announced this morning," a dealer said.
"There has been a lot of trade in (Russian) dollar Vnesh bonds, and in the min fins."
Another dealer said: "There're a lot of people with a lot of Russia paper on their books, but then investors like Russian risk."
"Some investors may be taking a punt that at $2.0 billion issue is too big and therefore short the bond," she added.
Russia launched its second dollar bond -- a $2.0 billion 10-year bond which will be priced to yield 375 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. The bond pays a coupon of 10.0 percent.
"Its a good yield, its what we thought it should be," a dealer said.
At 1130 GMT Russian VN US$ RUVNUSLNS=RR was bid at 91.50.
Russian MIN FIN 3 RU3E99=RR was bid at 89.875, MIN FIN 4 RU3E03=RR at 66.500 , Min FIN 5 RU3E08=RR at 47.75, RUSS MIN FIN 6 RU3E06=RR at 53.875 and RUSS MIN FIN 7 RU3E11=RR at 41.75.

BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said: "The line we're taking is that the yield curve in Russia is flat and the yield curve in Latin America is steep, so that if you look at a European comparison the new Russia looks good. But investors in New York might prefer the spread pick-up between five and 10-years in Latin America."
"The trade coming out of it is to switch at the long end into Latin America and at the short-end into Russia and the beneficiaries are the Russia 2001s and the Minfin 4's," Gray said.
There was also some profit-taking on Mexican risk in Tokyo ahead of the launch of a dollar bond for the country, a dealer said.
Mexico's PARS MX625L19=RR were bid at 78.25, Mexico's DISCs MXFLL19=RR at 93.375.
Mexico's $1.0 billion five-year global floating rate note is expected to be priced around 140 basis points over three-month LIBOR.
Bankers said the deal, expected on Thursday, would likely be callable in June 2000.
There was some cautiousness ahead of the release of U.S. economic data which was putting a dampner on bold positions, dealers said.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia survey is due out on Thursday.
"I think the Phil Fed will be strong and the market will shrug it off," BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said.
